---
title: "Merge MetS Extreme-Search Archetypes into Whole-Population Dataset"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This script merges the MetS extreme-search archetype results
(`Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft.MetS`, private cohort) into the whole-population
dataset (`Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft`, private cohort), creating a new grouping
variable:

- **0 = Healthy** — not part of the MetS extreme-search subset
- **1 = Mixed etiology** — in the MetS subset, but no archetype weight exceeds the threshold
- **2 = Extreme** — in the MetS subset, with max archetype weight above the threshold

The whole population's own `Archetypes 1-4` columns (a separate 4-archetype
decomposition) are **ignored** for this classification — they are left in
the data untouched but not used to derive the new group variable.

```{r parameters}
# ---- Edit these paths / threshold as needed ----
path_whole_population <- "Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft.RData"
path_mets             <- "Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft.MetS.RData"

id_col     <- "u3n_metabBiocrP500_ff4"          # unique subject ID column
arch_cols  <- c("Archetypes 1", "Archetypes 2", "Archetypes 3")  # MetS archetypes
threshold  <- 0.6                                # extreme vs. mixed cutoff

# All results/plots from this script are written here, in a folder specific
# to this RMD, so outputs from different analyses never collide.
output_dir <- "merge_MetS_groups_vf_results"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Load the two datasets

```{r load-data}
load(path_whole_population)   # loads object: Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft
load(path_mets)                # loads object: Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft.MetS

wp <- Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft
ms <- Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft.MetS

stopifnot(id_col %in% colnames(wp))
stopifnot(id_col %in% colnames(ms))
stopifnot(all(arch_cols %in% colnames(ms)))

dim(wp)
dim(ms)
```

```{r compute-groups}
ms_arch <- ms[, c(id_col, arch_cols)]

# Max archetype weight per subject, and which archetype it belongs to
ms_arch$max_weight         <- apply(ms_arch[, arch_cols], 1, max)
ms_arch$dominant_archetype <- arch_cols[apply(ms_arch[, arch_cols], 1, which.max)]
ms_arch$MetS_Group <- ifelse(ms_arch$max_weight > threshold, 2L, 1L)

table(ms_arch$MetS_Group)
summary(ms_arch$max_weight)
```

## Merge into the whole-population dataset

```{r merge}
merged <- wp
merged$MetS_Group <- 0L
merged$MetS_DominantArchetype <- NA_character_
merged$MetS_MaxArchetypeWeight <- NA_real_

match_idx <- match(merged[[id_col]], ms_arch[[id_col]])
in_mets   <- !is.na(match_idx)

merged$MetS_Group[in_mets]              <- ms_arch$MetS_Group[match_idx[in_mets]]
merged$MetS_DominantArchetype[in_mets]  <- ms_arch$dominant_archetype[match_idx[in_mets]]
merged$MetS_MaxArchetypeWeight[in_mets] <- ms_arch$max_weight[match_idx[in_mets]]

# Make it a labeled factor for convenience
merged$MetS_Group <- factor(
  merged$MetS_Group,
  levels = c(0, 1, 2),
  labels = c("Healthy", "Mixed", "Extreme")
)

table(merged$MetS_Group)
```

## Sanity checks

```{r checks}
# Every MetS-subset subject should be accounted for, and no extras introduced
stopifnot(sum(merged$MetS_Group != "Healthy") == nrow(ms))
stopifnot(all(merged[[id_col]][merged$MetS_Group != "Healthy"] %in% ms[[id_col]]))

dim(merged)
str(merged[, c(id_col, "MetS_Group", "MetS_DominantArchetype", "MetS_MaxArchetypeWeight")])
```

## Save outputs

```{r save}
Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft.WholePopulation <- merged
save(
  Merged.Metabolomics.Data.soft.WholePopulation,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "Merged_Metabolomics_Data_soft_WholePopulation_with_MetSGroup.RData")
)

write.csv(
  merged,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "Merged_Metabolomics_Data_soft_WholePopulation_with_MetSGroup.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```


### PCA
```{r PCA}
## =============================================================================
## Three-way PCA on clinical traits, using the `merged` data.frame you just
## =============================================================================

## ```{r define-clinical-traits-merged}
clinical_cols <- c(
  "u3lk_trin", "u3lk_krean", "u3lk_choln", "u3tglukfastn", "u3lk_ldln",
  "u3lk_hdln", "u3tquickin", "u3thoma2_ir", "u3thoma2_s",
  "u3tinsfastn", "u3h_crp", "u3tbmi", "u3tins2n", "u3twhrat", "u3tgewi",
  "u3l_hbavn", "u3tgluk2n", "u3thoma2_b", "u3tsysmm", "u3tdiamm", "u3tgroe"
)  # MetS_case dropped -- not present / would be redundant with MetS_Group

missing_clin <- setdiff(clinical_cols, names(merged))
if (length(missing_clin) > 0) {
  warning("These clinical columns are missing from `merged` and will be skipped: ",
          paste(missing_clin, collapse = ", "))
  clinical_cols <- setdiff(clinical_cols, missing_clin)
}
## ```

## ```{r pca-on-clinical-merged}
clinical_input <- merged[, clinical_cols, drop = FALSE]
clinical_input <- clinical_input[, sapply(clinical_input, function(x) is.numeric(x) && sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0), drop = FALSE]
clinical_input <- as.data.frame(lapply(clinical_input, function(x) {
  x[is.na(x)] <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)   # simple median impute; swap for your preferred method
  x
}))

pca_res_clin <- prcomp(clinical_input, center = TRUE)
var_explained_clin <- round(100 * pca_res_clin$sdev^2 / sum(pca_res_clin$sdev^2), 1)

pca_scores_clin <- as.data.frame(pca_res_clin$x[, 1:2])
pca_scores_clin[[id_col]] <- merged[[id_col]]
pca_scores_clin$MetS_Group             <- merged$MetS_Group
pca_scores_clin$MetS_DominantArchetype <- merged$MetS_DominantArchetype

# Build the plotting group: Healthy / Mixed / Extreme-<archetype>
pca_scores_clin$PlotGroup <- as.character(pca_scores_clin$MetS_Group)
extreme_idx <- pca_scores_clin$MetS_Group == "Extreme"
pca_scores_clin$PlotGroup[extreme_idx] <- pca_scores_clin$MetS_DominantArchetype[extreme_idx]
table(pca_scores_clin$PlotGroup)
## ```

## ```{r pca-plot-three-tier}
library(ggplot2)

group_colors <- c(
  "Healthy"       = "grey70",
  "Mixed"         = "#FF7F0E",   # orange
  "Archetypes 1"  = "#E64B35",   # red
  "Archetypes 2"  = "#4DBBD5",   # teal
  "Archetypes 3"  = "#00A087"    # green
)

# Draw order: Healthy first (background), then Mixed, then Extreme on top
plot_order <- c("Healthy", "Mixed", "Archetypes 1", "Archetypes 2", "Archetypes 3")
pca_scores_clin$PlotGroup <- factor(pca_scores_clin$PlotGroup, levels = plot_order)
pca_scores_clin <- pca_scores_clin[order(pca_scores_clin$PlotGroup), ]

p_pca_three_tier <- ggplot(pca_scores_clin, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = PlotGroup)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_colors, name = "Group", drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title    = "PCA of Clinical Traits: Healthy, Mixed, and Extreme MetS Subjects",
    subtitle = "Healthy (grey), Mixed etiology (orange), Extreme archetypes (colored)",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", var_explained_clin[1], "% variance)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", var_explained_clin[2], "% variance)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p_pca_three_tier)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "PCA_clinical_Healthy_Mixed_Extreme.pdf"),
  plot = p_pca_three_tier, width = 7.5, height = 5.5
)
## ```

## Regression analysis setup

Everything below uses **base R only** — no extra packages need to be
installed. All clinical traits and metabolites in this dataset are already
standardized (z-scored), so the regression coefficients below are
standardized betas (comparable in magnitude across metabolites/traits).

```{r reg-setup}
cols <- colnames(merged)
metabolite_cols <- cols[which(cols == "C0"):which(cols == "Choline")]
# (positive beta = higher in MetS cases).
stopifnot(all(merged$u3tmsidfup %in% c(1, 2)))
merged$MetS_case <- as.integer(merged$u3tmsidfup == 1)
table(merged$MetS_case, merged$u3tmsidfup)

# Continuous MetS-relevant clinical traits, plus the binary MetS case-status.
#  need a different model; recode/relevel them yourself if you want them in.)
mets_traits <- c("u3tgewi","u3tgroe","u3tbmi","u3twhrat","u3tsysmm","u3tdiamm",
                 "u3tglukfastn","u3tgluk2n","u3tinsfastn","u3tins2n",
                 "u3thoma2_b","u3thoma2_s","u3thoma2_ir","u3tquickin",
                 "u3lk_choln","u3lk_hdln","u3lk_ldln","u3lk_trin","u3lk_krean",
                 "u3l_hbavn","u3h_crp","MetS_case")
stopifnot(all(mets_traits %in% colnames(merged)))

# Full set of clinical traits used to define the MetS extreme-search
# subclustering (archetype decomposition), kept here as a code -> readable
# label dictionary. mets_traits above still drives the models actually
# fitted below; this is used purely to relabel plots/tables with
# human-readable trait names instead of raw variable codes.
traits = c(
    Age = "u3talteru",
    Gender = "u3csex",
    Weight = "u3tgewi",
    Height = "u3tgroe",
    BMI = "u3tbmi",
    WHO_BMI_Category = "u3tbmiwho",
    WHR = "u3twhrat",
    WHR_Category = "u3twhratc",
    SBP = "u3tsysmm",
    DBP = "u3tdiamm",
    Hypertension = "u3twhoish",
    Fasting_glucose = "u3tglukfastn",
    Glucose_2h = "u3tgluk2n",
    Diabetes_WHO = "u3tdm110y15",
    Fasting_serum_insulin = "u3tinsfastn",
    Insulin_2h = "u3tins2n",
    Metabolic_Syndrome_IDF = "u3tmsidfup",
    HOMA_Beta = "u3thoma2_b",
    HOMA_Sensitivity = "u3thoma2_s",
    HOMA_IR = "u3thoma2_ir",
    Insulin_Sensitivity_Quicki = "u3tquickin",
    Cholesterol = "u3lk_choln",
    HDL = "u3lk_hdln",
    LDL = "u3lk_ldln",
    TG = "u3lk_trin",
    Creatinine = "u3lk_krean",
    HbA1c = "u3l_hbavn",
    hsCRP = "u3h_crp"
  )
trait_label_lookup <- setNames(names(traits), traits)
trait_label_lookup["MetS_case"] <- "MetS_case"  # derived variable, not in `traits`

trait_label <- function(code) {
  lbl <- trait_label_lookup[code]
  ifelse(is.na(lbl), code, lbl)
}

age_col <- "u3talteru"
sex_col <- "u3csex"

length(metabolite_cols)  # number of metabolites
length(mets_traits)      # number of clinical traits (now includes MetS_case)

# small helper to pull a single term's beta/se/p out of a fitted lm
get_term_stats <- function(fit, term) {
  s <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  if (!term %in% rownames(s)) return(c(beta = NA, se = NA, p = NA))
  c(beta = s[term, 1], se = s[term, 2], p = s[term, 4])
}
```

For every metabolite x clinical trait pair, fit:

`metabolite ~ trait + age + sex`

and pull out the trait's beta/SE/p-value. P-values are FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg)
corrected **within each trait** (i.e. across the the metabolites tested for
that trait).

```{r step1-mwas}
run_mwas_continuous <- function(data, metabolites, trait, age_col, sex_col, extra_covars = NULL) {
  covars <- c(trait, age_col, sex_col, extra_covars)
  out <- vector("list", length(metabolites))
  for (i in seq_along(metabolites)) {
    mb <- metabolites[i]
    form <- as.formula(paste0("`", mb, "` ~ ", paste(covars, collapse = " + ")))
    fit <- lm(form, data = data)
    st <- get_term_stats(fit, trait)
    out[[i]] <- data.frame(metabolite = mb, trait = trait,
                            beta = st["beta"], se = st["se"], p = st["p"],
                            n = nobs(fit))
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}

mwas_list    <- lapply(mets_traits, function(tr)
                  run_mwas_continuous(merged, metabolite_cols, tr, age_col, sex_col))
mwas_results <- do.call(rbind, mwas_list)
rownames(mwas_results) <- NULL

mwas_results$q <- NA_real_
for (tr in mets_traits) {
  idx <- mwas_results$trait == tr
  mwas_results$q[idx] <- p.adjust(mwas_results$p[idx], method = "BH")
}

cat("Total metabolite-trait tests:", nrow(mwas_results), "\n")
cat("Significant at FDR q < 0.05:", sum(mwas_results$q < 0.05),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(mwas_results$q < 0.05)))
for (tr in c("u3lk_trin", "u3lk_hdln", "u3tbmi", "u3tglukfastn", "u3h_crp", "MetS_case")) {
  cat("\nTop hits for", trait_label(tr), "(", tr, "):\n")
  sub <- mwas_results[mwas_results$trait == tr, ]
  print(head(sub[order(sub$p), c("metabolite","beta","p","q")], 5), row.names = FALSE)
}

write.csv(mwas_results, file.path(output_dir, "step1_metabolite_trait_associations.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
```{r step1b-plot associations}
library(ggplot2)
sub <- mwas_results[mwas_results$trait %in% c("u3lk_trin","u3lk_hdln","u3tbmi","u3tglukfastn","u3h_crp","MetS_case"), ]

sub$direction <- with(sub, ifelse(q >= 0.05, "Not significant",
                            ifelse(beta > 0, "Positive (q < 0.05)", "Negative (q < 0.05)")))
sub$direction <- factor(sub$direction,
                         levels = c("Negative (q < 0.05)", "Not significant", "Positive (q < 0.05)"))

vpall= ggplot(sub, aes(x = beta, y = -log10(p), color = direction)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~trait, scales = "free", labeller = as_labeller(trait_label_lookup)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Negative (q < 0.05)" = "firebrick",
                                 "Not significant"      = "grey70",
                                 "Positive (q < 0.05)"  = "steelblue")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  labs(color = NULL, x = "Beta", y = expression(-log[10](p))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text  = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13)
  )

ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "volcano_plots.pdf"), plot = vpall, width = 15, height = 7)

``` 

For every metabolite, fit `metabolite ~ MetS_Group + age + sex` and extract
each group's contrast vs. Healthy (Mixed vs Healthy, Extreme vs Healthy).
FDR correction is applied across the the metabolites, separately for each
contrast.

```{r step2-group}
run_group_contrast <- function(data, metabolites, ref_level, age_col, sex_col) {
  d <- data
  d$MetS_Group <- relevel(d$MetS_Group, ref = ref_level)
  out <- vector("list", length(metabolites))
  for (i in seq_along(metabolites)) {
    mb <- metabolites[i]
    form <- as.formula(paste0("`", mb, "` ~ MetS_Group + ", age_col, " + ", sex_col))
    fit <- lm(form, data = d)
    row <- data.frame(metabolite = mb)
    for (lvl in setdiff(levels(d$MetS_Group), ref_level)) {
      term <- paste0("MetS_Group", lvl)
      st <- get_term_stats(fit, term)
      row[[paste0("beta_", lvl, "_vs_", ref_level)]] <- st["beta"]
      row[[paste0("se_",   lvl, "_vs_", ref_level)]] <- st["se"]
      row[[paste0("p_",    lvl, "_vs_", ref_level)]] <- st["p"]
    }
    out[[i]] <- row
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}

group_results <- run_group_contrast(merged, metabolite_cols, "Healthy", age_col, sex_col)

group_results$q_Mixed_vs_Healthy   <- p.adjust(group_results$p_Mixed_vs_Healthy,   method = "BH")
group_results$q_Extreme_vs_Healthy <- p.adjust(group_results$p_Extreme_vs_Healthy, method = "BH")

cat("Significant (q<0.05) Mixed vs Healthy:",   sum(group_results$q_Mixed_vs_Healthy   < 0.05), "\n")
cat("Significant (q<0.05) Extreme vs Healthy:", sum(group_results$q_Extreme_vs_Healthy < 0.05), "\n")

cat("\nTop hits, Mixed vs Healthy:\n")
print(head(group_results[order(group_results$p_Mixed_vs_Healthy),
      c("metabolite","beta_Mixed_vs_Healthy","q_Mixed_vs_Healthy")], 8), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nTop hits, Extreme vs Healthy:\n")
print(head(group_results[order(group_results$p_Extreme_vs_Healthy),
      c("metabolite","beta_Extreme_vs_Healthy","q_Extreme_vs_Healthy")], 8), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(group_results, file.path(output_dir, "step2_metabolite_group_associations.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Using the two contrasts from Step 2 (each thresholded at FDR q < 0.05), this
shows how much the "Mixed-vs-Healthy" and "Extreme-vs-Healthy" metabolite
signatures overlap with each other.

```{r step3-overlap}
set_MH <- group_results$metabolite[group_results$q_Mixed_vs_Healthy   < 0.05]
set_EH <- group_results$metabolite[group_results$q_Extreme_vs_Healthy < 0.05]

cat("Set sizes -> Mixed vs Healthy:", length(set_MH),
    " | Extreme vs Healthy:", length(set_EH), "\n")

n_MH_only <- length(setdiff(set_MH, set_EH))
n_EH_only <- length(setdiff(set_EH, set_MH))
n_both    <- length(intersect(set_MH, set_EH))

cat("Exclusive to Mixed-vs-Healthy:", n_MH_only, "\n")
cat("Exclusive to Extreme-vs-Healthy:", n_EH_only, "\n")
cat("Shared by both:", n_both, "\n")
draw_venn2 <- function(n1, n2, n12, labels = c("A", "B")) {
  plot(0, 0, type = "n", xlim = c(-1.8, 3.0), ylim = c(-2.1, 1.3),
       axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1)
  symbols(x = c(0, 1.1), y = c(0, 0), circles = c(1, 1),
          inches = FALSE, add = TRUE,
          fg = c("steelblue", "firebrick"), lwd = 2.5)
  text(-0.35, 0, n1, cex = 1.4)
  text(1.45, 0, n2, cex = 1.4)

This repeats the Step 1 metabolite-trait regressions, but adds an `Extreme`
indicator (Extreme vs everyone else) as an additional covariate:

`metabolite ~ trait + age + sex + Extreme`

Comparing the trait beta before vs. after shows how much of each
metabolite-trait association is confounded by / shared with extreme MetS
status.

```{r step4-adjust-extreme}
merged$Extreme <- as.integer(merged$MetS_Group == "Extreme")

mwas_list_adj <- lapply(mets_traits, function(tr)
                   run_mwas_continuous(merged, metabolite_cols, tr, age_col, sex_col,
                                       extra_covars = "Extreme"))
mwas_results_adj <- do.call(rbind, mwas_list_adj)
rownames(mwas_results_adj) <- NULL

mwas_results_adj$q <- NA_real_
for (tr in mets_traits) {
  idx <- mwas_results_adj$trait == tr
  mwas_results_adj$q[idx] <- p.adjust(mwas_results_adj$p[idx], method = "BH")
}

compare <- merge(
  mwas_results[,     c("metabolite","trait","beta","p","q")],
  mwas_results_adj[, c("metabolite","trait","beta","p","q")],
  by = c("metabolite","trait"), suffixes = c("_unadj","_adj")
)
compare$beta_change     <- compare$beta_adj - compare$beta_unadj
compare$pct_beta_change <- 100 * (compare$beta_adj - compare$beta_unadj) / abs(compare$beta_unadj)
compare$sig_unadj <- compare$q_unadj < 0.05
compare$sig_adj   <- compare$q_adj   < 0.05
compare$status <- ifelse(compare$sig_unadj & compare$sig_adj,  "Stays significant",
                   ifelse(compare$sig_unadj & !compare$sig_adj, "Loses significance",
                   ifelse(!compare$sig_unadj & compare$sig_adj, "Gains significance",
                                                                  "Stays non-sig")))

cat("How associations change once Extreme status is adjusted for:\n")
print(table(compare$status))

cat("\nMedian |beta change| (all pairs):", round(median(abs(compare$beta_change)), 4), "\n")
cat("Median |% beta change| (pairs significant before adjustment):",
    round(median(abs(compare$pct_beta_change[compare$sig_unadj])), 1), "%\n")

cat("\nWhich traits lose the most associations once Extreme is adjusted for:\n")
print(sort(table(compare$trait[compare$status == "Loses significance"]), decreasing = TRUE))

cat("\nLargest attenuations among pairs that lose significance:\n")
lost <- compare[compare$status == "Loses significance", ]
lost <- lost[order(-abs(lost$pct_beta_change)), ]
print(head(lost[, c("metabolite","trait","beta_unadj","beta_adj","pct_beta_change")], 10),
      row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(compare, file.path(output_dir, "step4_extreme_adjusted_comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

This plots every metabolite-trait beta from Step 1 (x-axis, unadjusted)
against the same pair's beta from Step 4 (y-axis, adjusted for Extreme).
Points on the dashed diagonal are unaffected by the adjustment; points that

Steps 2-3 found essentially **no** univariate metabolite differences between
Extreme and Mixed. That's a per-metabolite test, though — a joint,
multivariate model might still separate the groups even if no single
metabolite does. This section builds simple cross-validated logistic
regression classifiers (base R only — `glm()` plus a hand-rolled k-fold CV
and AUC, no extra packages) to test that directly, and to compare against
how well metabolites predict actual MetS case status for context.

For each comparison, a model is fit using:

- the top `k` metabolites (selected by univariate screening **within the
  training fold only**, to avoid leakage) + age + sex, and
- a baseline using age + sex alone (no metabolites),

evaluated by out-of-fold AUC over 10-fold stratified cross-validation.

```{r step6-predict-setup}
# Mann-Whitney based AUC (no pROC/ROCR needed)
auc_fn <- function(prob, label) {
  pos <- prob[label == 1]; neg <- prob[label == 0]
  n1 <- length(pos); n0 <- length(neg)
  r <- rank(c(pos, neg))
  (sum(r[1:n1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}

# k-fold stratified CV logistic regression with per-fold univariate feature screening
run_cv_logistic <- function(data, outcome_col, pos_label, metabolites, covars,
                             k_top = 8, n_folds = 10, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  d <- data
  y <- as.integer(d[[outcome_col]] == pos_label)
  n <- nrow(d)
  folds <- integer(n)
  for (lab in unique(y)) {
    idx <- which(y == lab)
    folds[idx] <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = length(idx)))
  }
  oof_pred <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  fold_feats <- vector("list", n_folds)
  for (f in 1:n_folds) {
    train_idx <- which(folds != f); test_idx <- which(folds == f)
    train <- d[train_idx, ]; test <- d[test_idx, ]
    ytr <- y[train_idx]
    if (k_top > 0) {
      pvals <- sapply(metabolites, function(mb) {
        fit <- tryCatch(stats::glm(ytr ~ train[[mb]], family = binomial), error = function(e) NULL)
        if (is.null(fit)) return(1)
        s <- summary(fit)$coefficients
        if (nrow(s) < 2) return(1)
        s[2, 4]
      })
      top_feats <- names(sort(pvals))[1:min(k_top, length(pvals))]
    } else {
      top_feats <- character(0)
    }
    fold_feats[[f]] <- top_feats
    form <- as.formula(paste("y_tr ~", paste(c(top_feats, covars), collapse = " + ")))
    train_df <- train[, c(top_feats, covars), drop = FALSE]
    train_df$y_tr <- ytr
    fit <- suppressWarnings(stats::glm(form, data = train_df, family = binomial))
    test_df <- test[, c(top_feats, covars), drop = FALSE]
    oof_pred[test_idx] <- suppressWarnings(stats::predict.glm(fit, newdata = test_df, type = "response"))
  }
  list(pred = oof_pred, y = y, auc = auc_fn(oof_pred, y), fold_feats = fold_feats)
}
covars <- c(age_col, sex_col)
```

```{r step6-predict-run}
em_subset <- merged[merged$MetS_Group %in% c("Mixed", "Extreme"), ]
em_subset$MetS_Group <- factor(em_subset$MetS_Group, levels = c("Mixed", "Extreme"))

eh_subset <- merged[merged$MetS_Group %in% c("Healthy", "Extreme"), ]
eh_subset$MetS_Group <- factor(eh_subset$MetS_Group, levels = c("Healthy", "Extreme"))

mh_subset <- merged[merged$MetS_Group %in% c("Healthy", "Mixed"), ]
mh_subset$MetS_Group <- factor(mh_subset$MetS_Group, levels = c("Healthy", "Mixed"))

comparisons <- list(
  list(name = "Extreme vs Mixed",   data = em_subset, pos = "Extreme"),
  list(name = "Extreme vs Healthy", data = eh_subset, pos = "Extreme"),
  list(name = "Mixed vs Healthy",   data = mh_subset, pos = "Mixed")
)

pred_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(comparisons, function(cmp) {
  full_model <- run_cv_logistic(cmp$data, "MetS_Group", cmp$pos, metabolite_cols, covars, k_top = 8)
  metab_only <- run_cv_logistic(cmp$data, "MetS_Group", cmp$pos, metabolite_cols, character(0), k_top = 8)
  baseline   <- run_cv_logistic(cmp$data, "MetS_Group", cmp$pos, metabolite_cols, covars, k_top = 0)
  data.frame(
    comparison        = cmp$name,
    n                  = nrow(cmp$data),
    auc_metab_age_sex  = round(full_model$auc, 3),
    auc_metab_only     = round(metab_only$auc, 3),
    auc_age_sex_only   = round(baseline$auc, 3)
  )
}))

print(pred_results, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(pred_results, file.path(output_dir, "step6_prediction_auc_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

**Interpretation:** metabolites are strong independent predictors of actual
MetS case status — for Extreme vs. Healthy and Mixed vs. Healthy, the
metabolites-only model (AUC ≈ 0.80-0.82) already outperforms age and sex
alone (AUC ≈ 0.66-0.70) by a wide margin, and combining metabolites with
age/sex pushes performance higher still (AUC ≈ 0.83-0.84) — metabolic
information is doing most of the work here, not demographics. In sharp
contrast, **no model — metabolites, age/sex, or both combined — meaningfully
separates Extreme from Mixed** (AUC ≈ 0.56-0.60 across all three models,
barely above the chance line at 0.5, and the combined model is no better
than age/sex alone). This corroborates the Step 2-3 finding from a
completely different angle: the 0.6 archetype-purity threshold does not
correspond to a learnable signature in metabolites *or* demographics, and is
not simply a power issue specific to univariate testing.

Step 6 selected its top-the metabolites independently within each CV fold, so
the *exact* feature set can vary fold to fold. To get a single, stable
answer to "which metabolites actually drive each model", this step counts
how often each metabolite was selected across the 10 folds (a simple,
package-free form of **stability selection** — a metabolite chosen in
10/10 folds is far more trustworthy than one chosen in 2/10), and reports
its effect size (odds ratio, p, FDR q) from a single age/sex-adjusted model
fit on the full comparison-specific data set.

```{r step7-stability-selection}
get_adj_univariate <- function(data, outcome_col, pos_label, metabolite, covars) {
  y <- as.integer(data[[outcome_col]] == pos_label)
  df <- data[, c(metabolite, covars)]
  df$y <- y
  form <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(c(metabolite, covars), collapse = " + ")))
  fit <- glm(form, data = df, family = binomial)
  s <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  c(OR = exp(s[metabolite, 1]), p = s[metabolite, 4])
}

posthoc_results <- list()
for (cmp in comparisons) {
  r <- run_cv_logistic(cmp$data, "MetS_Group", cmp$pos, metabolite_cols, covars, k_top = 8)
  freq <- sort(table(unlist(r$fold_feats)), decreasing = TRUE)
  top_n <- names(freq)[1:min(8, length(freq))]

  tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(top_n, function(mb) {
    st <- get_adj_univariate(cmp$data, "MetS_Group", cmp$pos, mb, covars)
    data.frame(metabolite = mb,
               times_selected_of_10 = as.integer(freq[mb]),
               OR = round(st["OR"], 3),
               p  = signif(st["p"], 3))
  }))
  tab$q <- round(p.adjust(tab$p, method = "BH"), 4)
  posthoc_results[[cmp$name]] <- tab

  cat("\n---", cmp$name, ": top metabolites driving the prediction ---\n")
  print(tab, row.names = FALSE)
}

write.csv(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(posthoc_results), function(nm) {
  cbind(comparison = nm, posthoc_results[[nm]])
})), file.path(output_dir, "step7_posthoc_predictive_metabolites.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

  tab <- posthoc_results[[nm]]
  tab <- tab[order(tab$times_selected_of_10), ]
  barplot(tab$times_selected_of_10, names.arg = tab$metabolite, horiz = TRUE,
          las = 1, col = "steelblue", xlim = c(0, 10),
          main = paste0(nm, ": metabolite selection frequency (10 CV folds)"),
          xlab = "Times selected across 10 folds",
          cex.names = 1.1, cex.axis = 1.2, cex.lab = 1.3, cex.main = 1.2,
          space = 0.6)   # adds space *within* each panel, between bars
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

dev.off()

``` 


**What drives each model:** for **Extreme vs Healthy** and **Mixed vs
Healthy**, the predictions are driven almost entirely by a small, highly
correlated cluster of **triglyceride (TG) and diglyceride (DG) species**
(e.g. `TG(16:0/34:0)`, `TG(18:0/34:2)`), each selected in 9-10/10 folds with
large, highly significant odds ratios (OR ≈ 4.3-5.5, q < 0.001) — consistent
with the strong lipid-trait signal already seen in Steps 1 and 2. For
**Extreme vs Mixed**, despite the model's weak overall AUC, the *same small
set* of metabolites is nonetheless picked consistently (`ADMA`, `AconAcid`
and `SDMA` in 10/10 folds; `C12` in 9/10) — and notably, these are exactly
the metabolites flagged in Step 5 as **gaining** significance once Extreme
status was adjusted for. Their individual effects are modest (OR 0.59-0.70)
and the resulting model still barely beats chance, but this is a genuine,
reproducible — if weak — signal, rather than noise: arginine-methylation
markers (ADMA/SDMA) and aconitate appear to track the archetype-purity
gradient even though no single metabolite, nor the full panel, separates
the two groups reliably enough to be clinically useful.
